claims.text: Sluggish atomic diffusion is typical of multi-element, near-equiatomic high-entropy systems.
Sluggish atomic diffusion is the key mechanism preserving the structural and chemical stability of high-entropy nanoparticles during high-temperature catalytic and thermoelectric service.
High activation barriers for atomic rearrangement kinetically stabilize a metastable, homogeneous elemental distribution.
Kinetic stabilization from high diffusion barriers minimizes phase separation and elemental segregation.
Rapid quenching produces initially disordered, metastable solid-solution nanoparticles with homogeneous elemental distributions.
A small tungsten or tantalum addition can be introduced while retaining a near-equiatomic overall composition.
Tungsten or tantalum is known to increase the activation energy for atomic movement in the proposed nanoparticles.
The complex multi-element lattice environment mediates the atomic diffusion barrier.
The refractory-metal dopant can alter the lattice diffusion barrier.
The complex energy landscape of high-entropy nanoparticles creates high activation barriers for atomic diffusion.
Adding a refractory-metal dopant will further increase diffusion barriers.
Increasing diffusion barriers will slow phase separation and compositional segregation at high temperature.
Doped nanoparticles will exhibit greater structural and chemical stability than identically processed undoped nanoparticles.
Doped nanoparticles will show less elemental segregation, phase separation, and lattice transformation during high-temperature exposure.
If the dopant unexpectedly lowers the diffusion barrier, phase separation may begin sooner.
The proposed interpretation is limited to initially solid-solution, near-equiatomic nanoparticles made by rapid quenching and tested within 773–1173 K or 473–1923 K.
Previous observations in high-entropy alloys associate sluggish diffusion with high-temperature behavior.
A lack of statistically significant dopant-induced change in diffusion activation energy or stability is defined as grounds to reject the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The predicted-outcome field says that a dopant-induced reduction in diffusion barrier accompanied by faster phase separation is an informative alternative observation, whereas the falsification rule classifies worse stability as rejection without conditioning on the measured barrier. A lower barrier together with worse stability would actually preserve the hypothesized barrier–stability correlation, even though it would refute the expectation that this dopant raises the barrier.
